Monroe County public housing inventory holds at 300 units in 2025
Monroe County reported 300 public housing units in 2025, unchanged from 2024.
Monroe County reported 300 public housing units in 2025, the same number as in 2024, according to HUD's Picture of Subsidized Households.
Tenant-based assistance covered 521 voucher units.
Monroe County had 200 project-based units through Project Based Section 8 and 202/PRAC.
All 300 public housing units in Monroe County were occupied, for an occupancy rate of 100%.
Monthly rent was 482, representing 28% of income.
Among Monroe County public housing residents, 23% were Hispanic, 53% were minority, 28% were Black non-Hispanic, 47% were White non-Hispanic, 2% were Asian/Pacific Islander non-Hispanic and 0% were Native American non-Hispanic.
Monroe County ranked 35th among Pennsylvania's 52 counties.
HUD-assisted housing programs generally reduce rent for low-income households that meet program eligibility requirements. HUD's Picture of Subsidized Households outlines three broad categories of assistance: public housing, tenant-based assistance and privately owned, project-based assistance. Local housing agencies own public housing, while tenant-based assistance, including housing vouchers, helps households rent homes in the private market. Project-based assistance is tied to specific privately owned properties with HUD rental-assistance contracts.
Households receiving HUD rental assistance generally pay rent equal to 30% of their income after deductions, while the federal government covers the remaining rent or rental costs. Eligibility is determined by HUD income limits that vary by location and household size, and applicants are usually placed on a waiting list until assistance is available.
